# CS 29.927 — Additional tests

> [!summary]
> CS 29.927 sets the additional tests for the rotor drive system of a large
> rotorcraft. It is a CS-29 specification, not a CS-E one, and the rotorcraft
> applicant owns it. Four regimes apply: dynamic and endurance testing, torque
> application tests where the pilot does not control engine output directly, a
> loss-of-lubrication test for each gearbox needed for safe flight, and 50
> overspeed runs. Three of them consume engine data that the engine applicant
> must supply.

## Requirement

The verbs below are CS-29's own. They bind the rotorcraft applicant, not the
engine applicant. See `## Bearing on this engine` for what reaches CS-E.

| Ref | Obligation | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| **(a)** | Perform any additional dynamic, endurance and operational tests, and vibratory investigations, needed to determine that the rotor drive mechanism is safe. | Required |
| **(b)** | Make the test below if turbine engine torque output to the transmission can exceed the highest engine or transmission torque limit, and that output is not directly controlled by the pilot under normal operating conditions. | Required |
| **(b)(1)** | With all engines operating, make 200 applications of torque, each of 10 seconds, at a torque at least equal to the lesser of the two values in (b)(1)(i) and (b)(1)(ii). | Required |
| **(b)(1)(i)** | The first candidate value is the maximum torque used in meeting CS 29.923 plus 10%. | Statement |
| **(b)(1)(ii)** | The second candidate value is the maximum torque attainable under probable operating conditions, assuming that torque limiting devices, if any, function properly. | Statement |
| **(b)(2)** | For a multi-engine rotorcraft, with each engine in turn becoming inoperative, apply to the remaining transmission torque inputs the maximum torque attainable under probable operating conditions, assuming that torque limiting devices, if any, function properly. Test each transmission input at that maximum torque for at least 15 minutes. | Required |
| **(c)** | Sub-points (c)(1) and (c)(2) apply to rotor drive system gearboxes required for continued safe flight or safe landing that have a pressurised normal-use lubrication system. | Statement |
| **(c)(1)** | Category A. Establish confidence that the rotor drive system has an in-flight operational endurance capability of at least 30 minutes after a failure of any one pressurised normal-use lubrication system. | Required |
| **(c)(1)** | Conduct, for each such gearbox, a test simulating the effect of the most severe failure mode of the normal-use lubrication system, as determined by the failure analysis of CS 29.917(b). | Required |
| **(c)(1)** | Make the test duration dependent upon the number of tests and the component condition after the test. | Required |
| **(c)(1)** | Begin the test upon the indication to the flight crew that a lubrication failure has occurred. Load it consistently with 1 minute at maximum continuous power, then the minimum power needed for continued flight at the rotorcraft maximum gross weight. End it with a 45-second out of ground effect (OGE) hover to simulate a landing phase. | Required |
| **(c)(1)** | Substantiate by the test results the maximum period of operation following loss of lubrication, by extended test duration, multiple test specimens, or another approach prescribed by the applicant and accepted by EASA. Support the procedures published in the rotorcraft flight manual (RFM). | Required |
| **(c)(1)** | Flight durations longer than 30 minutes may be demonstrated by a correspondingly longer test, with appropriate margin and substantiation. | Permitted |
| **(c)(2)** | Category B. Establish confidence that the rotor drive system has an in-flight operational endurance capability to complete an autorotation descent and landing after a failure of any one pressurised normal-use lubrication system. | Required |
| **(c)(2)** | Conduct, for each gearbox needed for safe autorotation descent or safe landing, a test of at least 16 minutes and 15 seconds following the most severe failure mode of the normal-use lubrication system, as determined by the failure analysis of CS 29.917(b). | Required |
| **(c)(2)** | Begin the test upon the indication to the flight crew that a lubrication failure has occurred, and load it consistently with 1 minute at maximum continuous power. | Required |
| **(c)(2)** | After that minute, the input torque should be reduced to simulate autorotation for 15 minutes. | Recommended |
| **(c)(2)** | Complete the test by applying an input torque to simulate a minimum power landing for approximately 15 seconds. | Required |
| **(d)** | Subject the rotor drive system to 50 overspeed runs, each 30 ± 3 seconds in duration, at not less than the higher of the rotational speed expected from an engine control device failure or 105% of the maximum rotational speed, including transients, expected in service. | Required |
| **(d)** | The rotational speed limits of speed and torque limiting devices need not be exceeded, where those devices are installed, are independent of the normal engine control, and are shown to be reliable. | Relief |
| **(d)(1)** | Alternate the overspeed runs with stabilising runs of 1 to 5 minutes each, at 60 to 80% of maximum continuous speed. | Required |
| **(d)(2)** | Accomplish acceleration and deceleration in no more than 10 seconds, except where the maximum engine acceleration rate requires more. Do not deduct the time for changing speeds from the specified overspeed run time. | Required |
| **(d)(3)** | Make the overspeed runs with the rotors in the flattest pitch for smooth operation. | Required |
| **(e)** | Conduct the tests of (b) and (d) on the rotorcraft, and absorb the torque by the rotors to be installed. | Required |
| **(e)** | Other ground or flight test facilities with other appropriate methods of torque absorption may be used, if the conditions of support and vibration closely simulate those of a test on the rotorcraft. | Permitted |
| **(f)** | Conduct each test of this paragraph without intervening disassembly. Each part tested must be in a serviceable condition at the conclusion of the test, except for the lubrication system failure test of (c). | Required |

Sub-point (c)(2) uses "should" for the autorotation phase inside an otherwise
mandatory test. CS-29 is a specification, so the verb is a recommendation, not
an accepted means. The surrounding obligations use "shall" and stay mandatory.

Sub-point (d)(2) forbids a deduction: the time spent changing speed "may not be
deducted from the specified time for the overspeed runs" [ext CS 29.927(d)(2)].
The row records that as Required, because the constraint is mandatory.

Category A and Category B are rotorcraft certification categories. They decide
which of (c)(1) and (c)(2) applies. The category is not an engine declaration
and `engine_profile.md` does not carry one.

## Bearing on this engine

CS 29.927 creates no CS-E obligation. The tests are run on the rotor drive
system, which is not part of the engine type design. The paragraph still
matters, because three of its test conditions are defined by engine data.

The torque application tests assume the engine's torque limiting devices work.
Both (b)(1)(ii) and (b)(2) set the test torque at "the maximum torque attainable
under probable operating conditions, assuming that torque limiting devices, if
any, function properly" [ext CS 29.927(b)(2)]. Where that limiter is the EECS,
its integrity is engine-side evidence under [[CS-E 50]], and its failure
behaviour reaches the safety analysis of [[CS-E 510]].

The overspeed test takes its speed from an engine failure case. Sub-point (d)
uses "the higher of the rotational speed to be expected from an engine control
device failure or 105% of the maximum rotational speed, including transients, to
be expected in service" [ext CS 29.927(d)]. The first figure comes from the
engine control system assessment, and must reach the installer through the
installation instructions required by [[CS-E 20]].

The OEI case in (b)(2) runs for at least 15 minutes with one engine inoperative.
The torque available from the remaining engines over that period follows from
the ratings declared under [[CS-E 40]], not from the short OEI ratings: 15
minutes exceeds both the 30-Second and the 2-Minute OEI Power Ratings.

[VERIFY: whether the rotorcraft applicant runs the 15-minute input test of
CS 29.927(b)(2) at Continuous OEI torque, or at a higher transient value. CS-29
says only "the maximum torque attainable under probable operating conditions",
and the engine's declared ratings do not settle which condition that is.]

The relief in (d) is engine-dependent in the same way. Speed and torque limiting
devices escape the overspeed sweep only where they are "independent of the normal
engine control" [ext CS 29.927(d)]. A full-authority EECS that provides both the
control and the limit does not meet that condition on its own.

Two engine tests look similar to these and are separate. [CS-E 820] is the
engine Over-torque Test and [CS-E 830] is the Maximum Engine Over-speed test.
Both are run on the engine and prove an engine limit. CS 29.927 proves the
transmission behind it.

The loss-of-lubrication regime in (c) covers the gearbox's own pressurised
lubrication system. It is not the engine Oil System of [CS-E 570], and no CS-E
obligation follows from it.

[VERIFY: whether the installation is certificated under CS-29 or CS-27. The
counterpart paragraph [[CS 27.927]] is materially different, in particular for
loss of lubrication. [[CS-E 30]] carries the same open item.]
